question: What feed solution viscosity did the Indigofera dye solution with maltodextrin have?
rendered:
Standardisation of natural dye powders via spray drying: initial physicochemical characterisation, page 3

The feed solution was prepared by dispersing 200 g of Indigofera paste into 740 g of distilled water at room temperature. Dispersion was carried out using a mechanical stirrer at a medium speed for 15 minutes to obtain a homogeneous and agglomeration-free suspension. Next, 90 g of maltodextrin (15% w/w) was gradually added to the suspension as a carrier, with continuous stirring until the maltodextrin was hydrated and completely dispersed. Aer all the components were homogeneously mixed, the solution volume was adjusted to reach a total mass of approximately 1000 g, and the solution was allowed to stand until the viscosity was stabilized. 

The addition of maltodextrin into the solution provided feed solution viscosities of around 4.5 cSt, 3.7 cSt, and 5.2 cSt for Tingi bark, Tegeran wood, and Indigofera, respectively.

The Indigofera dye solution with maltodextrin had a viscosity of 5.2 cSt.
